newsitem.title: UGANDA: Tanzania, Uganda airlines agree merger.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania, Uganda airlines agree merger.

text.p: The governments of Tanzania and Uganda have agreed on the merger of their airlines with Alliance Air and this will supersede privatisation plans, documents from a meeting between Ugandan and Tanzanian officials showed.

A study on the deal must be finalised by end-June, according to minutes taken at a meeting between Ugandan Works, Transport and Communications Minister John Nasasira and Tanzanian Transport and Communications Minister William Kulia.

"In that regard, measures should be taken to obtain optimum economic advantage by integrating the three airlines -- Alliance Air, Uganda Airlines and Air Tanzania -- and that this process should proceed or take place before privatisation," a resolution at the meeting on February 17 showed.
The minutes were passed to Reuters on Thursday. Officially, Tanzanian and Ugandan governments have declined to comment.
The two governments are partners in Alliance Air with South African Airways (SAA). They each own a 30 percent stake in Alliance, with SAA owning 40 percent.
SAA provides technical services to the airline which flies twice a week to London and between Dar es Salaam, Entebbe and Johannesburg.

The minutes said: "In order to facilitate the process of a merger in the context of a privatisation policy, a consultant should be immediately appointed to make appropriate recommendations on methodology and institutional structure of the integrated airline."
They added: "The approved terms of reference shall be completed by 10th March 1997 and the consultant appointed by end of March 1997 to facilitate the study by the end of June."
The ministers asked the privatisation bodies in their respective coountries to coordinate their activities to ensure that government interests were taken into account.
Alliance company secretary Fred Obbo told Reuters on Tuesday from the firm's head office in the Ugandan capital, Kampala, the national airlines would cease to exist as separate entities.
"We will just have one airline," Obbo said.
Air Tanzania and Uganda Airlines have since the start-up of Alliance in 1995 been limited to flying routes within Africa.

Air Tanzania owns two Boeing 737-200 medium haul airliners, each with 130 seats. It also has a Fokker F-27 for domestic routes. Details on what aircraft Uganda Airlines owns were not immediately available.
